summary: ID token subject prefix mismatch causes intermittent 403 on service token-refresh in private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
Customers experiencing intermittent 403 responses when a service account attempts token-refresh via the private control plane. Errors surface in production us-east and affect background job processing for BrightBank.

Impact:
- Several scheduled worker jobs (payment reconciliation) are failing to authenticate, causing near-real-time processing delays (~15-30 min backlog).
- Authentication failures are intermittent: ~1-3% of token refresh attempts return 403.

Environment:
- Private deployment (BrightBank VPC, Private control plane)
- Region: us-east
- Identity provider: customer's internal OIDC provider relayed by identity-proxy
- Affected clients: service-to-service token refresh (client credentials flow with id_token exchange retained for auditing)

Steps to reproduce:
1) From inside BrightBank VPC, call /v1/token/refresh with service account refresh token using identity-proxy as relay.
2) Observe 200 for most requests; ~1-3% return 403 with body: {"error":"invalid_token","detail":"subject mismatch"}.
3) Correlate with identity-proxy logs and control-plane token-exchange traces.

Expected behavior:
- Token refresh should succeed for valid refresh tokens and return new access tokens consistently.

Actual behavior:
- Intermittent 403 from token-exchange with message indicating id_token subject mismatch.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "WARN auth: id_token sub 'svc-ops-79' does not match cached subject 'svc-ops-hr' for client_id 'brightbank-payments'"
- control-plane: "ERROR token-exchange: incoming id_token subject prefix 'svc-ops-' differs from allowed prefix 'svc_reports-' -> reject"

Additional notes:
- This started after BrightBank rotated a naming prefix in their AD connectors the week of 2026-03-02. Not all service accounts were updated to the new subject namespace.

Hypothesis: upstream token-issuance is inconsistent during rotation causing subject prefix variance and name-based auth policy rejecting when prefixes differ.

Control-plane currently enforces strict subject-prefix policy during token refresh to prevent privilege escalation across namespaces. This is rejecting valid rotated tokens when subject namespace temporarily diverges.

Planning follow-up fix to make subject-prefix policy tolerant during rotation windows and add signal to console.

investigation: Hypothesis: The identity provider rotation changed the subject namespace for service accounts (prefix change). Control-plane subject-prefix policy rejects requests when id_token.sub doesn't match the expected tenant-scoped namespace. Evidence: identity-proxy logs show alternating subject prefixes for the same client_id during rotation window. Trace links: https://observability.redwood.prod/traces?trace=req-20260310-87a. Metrics: token-exchange 403 spike correlated to 2026-03-02 AD rotation event. Reproduction steps executed in staging with replay tokens replicated the 403 behavior. Root cause: strict enforcement of exact subject-prefix mapping without accounting for rotation windows and multi-prefix allowlist per tenant.
resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-03-12: tenant-scoped temporary allowlist added to control-plane for BrightBank to accept both old and new subject prefixes. Observed immediate reduction in failures (<0.1%).

Permanent fix plan:
- Deploy tolerant subject-prefix matching logic that supports a short-lived rotation window per tenant and logs rotation diagnostics (ENG-2012). PR created: https://github.com/redwood/inference-auth/pull/298.
- Add console signal and alerting when subject-prefix variance exceeds threshold (OPS-894).
- Post-deploy: perform coordinated tenant rotation test with BrightBank to validate.

Follow-ups:
- Runbook update: add section for tenant prefix rotations and allowlist procedure.
- Customer communication: notify BrightBank when permanent fix is deployed and recommend schedule for future rotations.

Ticket outcome: mitigation in place; awaiting deployment of PR and QA.
